name: Fintan the salmon

attributes.attribute: one possible source of his pool
another possible source of his pool

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fintan the salmon was also called Goll Essa Ruaid. The name means the one-eyed one of the red waterfall. He swam in a pool at the source of an Irish river. The river was either the Boyne or the Erne. He nibbled the hazel nuts that dropped from magical bushes. The druid Finneces caught him. The hero Fionn mac Cumhaill ate him by accident. Fionn then gained immense wisdom.

okr.objective: Fintan the salmon carries the wisdom that Fionn mac Cumhaill consumed.
key_results: Fintan the salmon is also called Goll Essa Ruaid.
He swam at the source of the Boyne or the Erne.
He ate hazel nuts from magical bushes.
Fionn mac Cumhaill gained wisdom by eating him.
